amenitiesDescription:
The amenity program is arranged by level rather than stacked on one floor. A private lobby lounge sits at grade, with a sculptural staircase rising to the mezzanine, where a wellness spa holds his-and-hers sanctuaries with steam and sauna rooms, a co-ed hammam, and private treatment suites. A private dining room on the same level serves smaller gatherings. The Zen level pairs a fitness center with an adjoining outdoor garden.

The roof carries the social program: a lap pool, a reflection pool, a cold plunge and Jacuzzi, private cabanas and sun decks, and a rooftop lounge with a staffed bar and terraces looking across the South Gables skyline. Building services include a doorman and hospitality-trained concierge, 24/7 valet and attended lobby, 24-hour security, in-residence mail delivery, laundry and dry cleaning, pet care and dog walking, grocery delivery, and restaurant reservations. Housekeeping, private chefs, and wellness treatments are arranged à la carte through the concierge. Private storage is available for purchase.
description: Ponce Park is a 58-residence, 11-story condominium at 3000 Ponce de Leon Boulevard in Coral Gables, facing the city-owned Ponce Circle Park. Developed by Allen Morris Company with architecture by John Cunningham of Zyscovich and interiors by Meyer Davis, the building carries Coral Gables' Mediterranean Revival vocabulary into a contemporary neoclassical facade. Residences run from two to five bedrooms across roughly 1,900 to more than 6,500 square feet, with private elevators, ceilings of 11 to 12 feet, and 11-foot-deep terraces fitted with summer kitchens. Ground level holds 25,000 square feet of retail anchored by Quintín Ultramarinos, the first United States outpost of the Madrid all-day dining institution. The 1.2-acre project broke ground in December 2025, with 40 percent of the residences pre-sold at that point, and is expected to complete in early 2028.

investmentIntelligence.thesis: Ponce Park is a scarcity play on a submarket that rarely produces large new condominiums. Coral Gables' design review and low-rise character have kept new supply thin for a decade, and the 2024 rezoning that permitted this building took four years and two rejected proposals to secure. What buyers get is a 58-home building averaging well above 2,000 square feet, with a private elevator per residence, in a city where comparable product mostly means resale in older Mediterranean buildings. The ground floor is doing real work: Quintín Ultramarinos is an established Madrid operator rather than a speculative tenant, and the $11 million Ponce Circle Park renovation Allen Morris is helping fund improves the building's own frontage. The $132.5 million Bank OZK loan closing one month after groundbreaking is the strongest available signal that an outside underwriter has tested the numbers.

investmentThesis: Coral Gables has very little new condominium supply and almost none at this scale of residence. Fifty-eight homes averaging well over 2,000 square feet is a different product from the compact-unit towers rising in Brickell and Edgewater, and it is aimed at a buyer moving within the Gables rather than into it. Allen Morris Company is Coral Gables-based and has been assembling and entitling this site since 2019, taking it through four years of city review that reduced the unit count and enlarged the homes. Bank OZK closed a $132.5 million construction loan in January 2026, roughly one month after groundbreaking, which is meaningful validation in a lending market that has grown selective on Miami condominium construction. The ground floor is the differentiator: 25,000 square feet of retail anchored by Quintín Ultramarinos, the first United States location for Grupo Paraguas, whose Madrid original has run since 2015. Allen Morris is also contributing to the $11 million renovation of Ponce Circle Park across the street, which upgrades the building's own outlook. The city's estimate has since risen to $11.2 million and the split on the funding gap is still being finalized.

neighborhoodMap.caption: The developer's neighborhood guide plots 66 destinations around the site: 22 restaurants, the Miracle Mile and Giralda Plaza retail corridors, Shops at Merrick Park, the Biltmore and Granada golf courses, the Venetian Pool, and the Coconut Grove marinas on Biscayne Bay. Ponce Circle Park, whose $11 million renovation Allen Morris is helping fund, sits directly across Ponce de Leon Boulevard.

residenceContent: A neoclassical facade on Ponce de Leon Boulevard, drawn from the Mediterranean Revival vocabulary that has governed Coral Gables since Merrick laid it out. John Cunningham's elevation reads as stone and shadow rather than glass, with deep arcades at street level opening onto Ponce Circle Park. The residences sit above, each reached by a private elevator that opens into a wood-paneled foyer and a set of double doors. Ceilings run 11 to 12 feet. Floors are European oak, with natural stone through the bathrooms and custom Italian cabinetry in the walk-in closets. Terraces run 11 feet deep, finished in tile rather than exposed concrete and fitted with summer kitchens, so the outdoor room works as an extension of the interior rather than a balcony. Kitchens are Meyer Davis: handcrafted Italian wood cabinetry, Italian stone counters with double waterfall edges, a Sub-Zero and Wolf suite built around a 60-inch refrigerator and integrated wine preservation, and La Cornue 60-inch gas ranges in select residences. Full-height pantries and concealed appliance storage keep the room quiet. Smart-home technology is integrated throughout, and select residences add wine cellars, studies, offices, and libraries.
